title: Migrate Blazor E2E tests to Components.Testing
body:
## Summary

We introduced `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing` (#65958, #66394, #68289) to provide a modern, Playwright based end-to-end testing infrastructure for Blazor applications. This issue tracks incrementally migrating our existing Selenium-based E2E test suite (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests`) to `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing`, cleaning up our `testassets`, and evolving the library into a public package and agent skill that Blazor developers can use to test their own applications.

## Goals

1. **Incrementally migrate existing E2E tests to `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing`:**
   - Replace legacy Selenium tests with readable, fast Playwright tests using `ServerFixture`, YARP proxy routing, and cross-process service overrides (following a developer experience similar to `WebApplicationFactory`).
   - Enable running E2E tests across multiple browsers and make it easy for developers and coding agents to run and filter E2E tests locally.
2. **Avoid test-logic flakiness by design:**
   - Tests migrated to the new infrastructure must be deterministic and not rely on arbitrary sleeps and polling.
   - Instead of one-off hacks in individual tests, we will build first-class synchronization primitives, lifecycle hooks, and readiness gates into the framework and testing library (for example, observing prerendered DOM state before interactive activation, waiting for Blazor runtime startup, enhanced navigation completion, or interactive handoff).
3. **Standardize framework test hooks for public consumption:**
   - As we migrate tests that currently rely on internal workarounds to inspect or gate framework state, replace those workarounds with clean, supported entry points and diagnostic channels.
   - Because `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing` is intended to ship as a supported package for Blazor developers, the primitives we add should be designed for public consumption.
4. **Clean up and reorganize `testassets` and test structure:**
   - Re-evaluate and simplify the existing E2E `testassets` projects that have accumulated overlapping scenarios over time so they are easier to navigate and debug.
   - Support running selected test subsets across different hosting configurations (such as Server vs. WebAssembly) and isolated process configurations (such as different `AppContext` switches or Native AOT via #68289).
   - Improve CI and Helix execution partitioning (for example, attribute-driven test groups/traits and Helix job generation similar to `Wasm.Build.Tests` in `dotnet/runtime`).
5. **Better diagnostics, CI reliability, and developer/agent ergonomics:**
   - Leverage built-in Playwright tracing and structured diagnostics on failure.
   - Keep overall suite execution time low while separating genuine infrastructure failures (recoverable via selective test re-runs) from test-logic races.
   - Ship a reusable E2E testing skill and guidance so customers and agents can adopt `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing` in their own projects.

## Open Questions / Further Exploration

- How to best structure multi-environment and isolated `AppContext` test permutations in MSBuild and Helix.
- Whether and how to extend the testing model to cover `BlazorWebView` / Hybrid scenarios (WinForms, WPF, MAUI).
- Integration with CI selective retry / Test Monitor for transient machine or network failures.

title: JsonPatch: `move` still adds the value at `path` when removing it from `from` failed
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

[`ObjectAdapter.Move`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b63914031c4d795130a5a7873f6e8e4865139358/src/Features/JsonPatch/src/Adapters/ObjectAdapter.cs#L99-L116) reads the value at `from`, then calls `Remove(operation.from, ...)`, then `Add(operation.path, ...)`. The private `Remove` reports a failure through the error callback and returns `void`, so `Move` cannot tell that the removal failed and adds the value at `path` anyway.

When `ApplyTo` runs without an error callback, the default reporter throws a `JsonPatchException` from `Remove`, so nothing is added. With a callback, the value is added, and MVC's `ApplyTo(model, ModelState)` always passes one. The `move` is then reported as an error and also applied as a copy: the value is still at `from` and now also at `path`. RFC 6902 §4.4 defines `move` as a removal from `from` followed by an add at `path`. When the removal fails the operation fails, and nothing should be added.

A simple way to hit it is a property JSON Patch can read but not write, such as a get-only property or one with a private setter (compare #51514). `remove` refuses it with "could not be updated", and `move` from it copies it.

`Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.SystemTextJson` has the same code in its [`ObjectAdapter.Move`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b63914031c4d795130a5a7873f6e8e4865139358/src/Features/JsonPatch.SystemTextJson/src/Adapters/ObjectAdapter.cs#L101-L115) and behaves the same.

Newtonsoft.Json package (from the linked repro; the model has `public string Reference { get; } = "R-1";` and `public string? Note { get; set; }`):

```
== 5. move adds the value at path after removing it from from failed: a copy, not a move
5a. move from a get-only property, errors logged (as ApplyTo(model, ModelState))
  patch [{"op":"move","from":"/reference","path":"/note"}] -> JsonPatchError: The property at path 'reference' could not be updated. (operation path '/note', from '/reference'); then reference R-1, note R-1
5b. the same, ApplyTo(model) without an error callback
  patch [{"op":"move","from":"/reference","path":"/note"}] -> threw Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.Exceptions.JsonPatchException: The property at path 'reference' could not be updated.; then reference R-1, note null
        at Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.Adapters.ObjectAdapter.Remove(String path, Object objectToApplyTo, Operation operationToReport)
5c. for comparison, remove of the same property
  patch [{"op":"remove","path":"/reference"}] -> JsonPatchError: The property at path 'reference' could not be updated. (operation path '/reference', from ''); then reference R-1, note null
```

System.Text.Json package, 10.0.13:

```csharp
using System.Text.Json;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.SystemTextJson;

var options = new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web);
var doc = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<JsonPatchDocument<M>>("""[{"op":"move","from":"/reference","path":"/note"}]""", options)!;
var m = new M();
doc.ApplyTo(m, e => Console.WriteLine("JsonPatchError: " + e.ErrorMessage));
Console.WriteLine($"reference {m.Reference}, note {m.Note ?? "null"}");

public sealed class M { public string Reference { get; } = "R-1"; public string? Note { get; set; } }
```

```
JsonPatchError: The property at path 'reference' could not be updated.
reference R-1, note R-1
```

### Expected Behavior

When the removal from `from` fails, `move` reports the error and adds nothing at `path`, whether or not an error callback is given. `note` stays `null` in 5a, as it does in 5b.

### Steps To Reproduce

https://github.com/AdCodicem/dotnet-upstream-repros/tree/main/aspnetcore-jsonpatch-newtonsoft (section 5 of the output). It is a console app referencing only `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch`. Run it with `./repro.sh` for .NET 10, or with `REPRO_TFM=net11.0 ./repro.sh` for .NET 11 RC1. The output of both runs is committed next to it. The System.Text.Json snippet above is complete as it stands, with a reference to `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.SystemTextJson`.

### Exceptions (if any)

None with an error callback: the error is reported and the value is copied anyway (5a).

### .NET Version

10.0.402

### Anything else?

- Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 10.0.13 with Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3 on .NET 10. Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 with Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4 on SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128, with the same output. Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.SystemTextJson 10.0.13 on .NET 10. Windows 11.
- The code is identical on main and release/10.0 in both packages.

Investigation and write-up assisted by Claude (Anthropic); the linked repro was run on Windows 11 (10.0.26200) with .NET SDK 10.0.402, Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 10.0.13, Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.SystemTextJson 10.0.13 and Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3, and with .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128, Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 and Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4, and I reviewed this report.

title: JsonPatch (Newtonsoft.Json): values are converted under the `ContractResolver` alone, and the converter's error is swallowed
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

In `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch` (the Newtonsoft.Json-based package), any `add`, `replace` or `test` value that is not already of the target type goes through [`ConversionResultProvider.ConvertTo`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b63914031c4d795130a5a7873f6e8e4865139358/src/Features/JsonPatch/src/Internal/ConversionResultProvider.cs#L21-L56). That method writes the value to JSON and reads it back under `new JsonSerializerSettings { ContractResolver = contractResolver }`. Two problems follow:

1. **Every setting except the resolver is dropped.** A `JsonPatchDocument` carries only a `ContractResolver`, and [`NewtonsoftJsonPatchInputFormatter`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b63914031c4d795130a5a7873f6e8e4865139358/src/Mvc/Mvc.NewtonsoftJson/src/NewtonsoftJsonPatchInputFormatter.cs#L71-L74) copies only that from `MvcNewtonsoftJsonOptions.SerializerSettings`. So `Converters`, `DateTimeZoneHandling`, `FloatParseHandling`, `DateParseHandling`, `Culture` and the rest apply to a request body and not to the same value in a patch.
2. **The exception is swallowed.** The bare `catch` turns any converter error into "The value '…' is invalid for target location.". The message the converter wrote for the client is lost.

The repro reads the same JSON as a plain body and as a patch value under the same settings. It gives the patch document the settings' resolver, as the input formatter does, and applies it with an error callback, as `ApplyTo(model, ModelState)` does:

```
1d. DateTime, DateTimeZoneHandling.Utc
  body  {"shippedAt":"2024-05-01T10:00:00+05:30"} -> 2024-05-01T04:30:00.0000000Z (Kind Utc)
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/shippedAt","value":"2024-05-01T10:00:00+05:30"}] -> 2024-05-01T06:30:00.0000000+02:00 (Kind Local)
1e. a [JsonConverter] reading reader.Value, FloatParseHandling.Decimal
  body  {"price":0.12345678901234567890} -> 0.12345678901234567890
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/price","value":0.12345678901234567890}] -> 0.123456789012346
1f. a converter of JsonSerializerSettings.Converters
  body  {"discount":15} -> 15
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/discount","value":15}] -> JsonPatchError: The value '15' is invalid for target location. (operation path '/discount', from '')
1g. the exception of the contract resolver's converter
  body  {"sku":"abc"} -> JsonSerializationException: A SKU has exactly 8 characters.
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/sku","value":"abc"}] -> JsonPatchError: The value 'abc' is invalid for target location. (operation path '/sku', from '')
```

In 1e, the document itself was read under `FloatParseHandling.Decimal`, so the value reached `ConvertTo` as the exact `decimal`. The round trip under fresh settings then hands the type's converter a `double`.

For context, under Newtonsoft.Json's default settings, which `AddNewtonsoftJson()` keeps, a plain `DateTimeOffset` takes the server's offset and a `decimal` loses digits. A request body keeps both:

```
1a. DateTimeOffset, Newtonsoft.Json's default settings
  body  {"placedAt":"2024-05-01T10:00:00+05:30"} -> 2024-05-01T10:00:00.0000000+05:30
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/placedAt","value":"2024-05-01T10:00:00+05:30"}] -> 2024-05-01T06:30:00.0000000+02:00
1b. decimal, Newtonsoft.Json's default settings
  body  {"total":0.12345678901234567890} -> 0.12345678901234567890
  patch [{"op":"replace","path":"/total","value":0.12345678901234567890}] -> 0.12345678901234568
```

These two come mostly from `Operation.value` being read as `object` (a local `DateTime`, a `double`) before the target type is known. An application can avoid them for plain types with `DateParseHandling.None` and `FloatParseHandling.Decimal` (case 1c of the repro). It cannot avoid them for a type read by a converter (1e), because `ConvertTo` drops those settings again. #40916 (`DateOnly`: "The value '01/02/2024 00:00:00' is invalid for target location.") looks like the same mechanism.

### Expected Behavior

- A patch value is converted under the application's serializer settings, so each `patch` line above gives what its `body` line gives. One way would be for the document to carry the `JsonSerializerSettings` (or a `JsonSerializer`) and for the input formatter to set it, as it sets `ContractResolver` today. `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.SystemTextJson` already converts under the application's `JsonSerializerOptions`.
- When the converter throws a `JsonException`, the `JsonPatchError` carries its message, or at least does not hide it. Note that `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch.SystemTextJson`'s `ConversionResultProvider` has the same bare `catch`.

### Steps To Reproduce

https://github.com/AdCodicem/dotnet-upstream-repros/tree/main/aspnetcore-jsonpatch-newtonsoft (section 1 of the output). It is a console app referencing only `Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch`. Run it with `./repro.sh` for .NET 10, or with `REPRO_TFM=net11.0 ./repro.sh` for .NET 11 RC1. The output of both runs is committed next to it; the machine's UTC offset was +02:00.

### Exceptions (if any)

None escape. The converter's `JsonSerializationException: A SKU has exactly 8 characters.` is caught and replaced (case 1g).

### .NET Version

10.0.402

### Anything else?

- Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 10.0.13 with Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3 on .NET 10. Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 (and 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105) with Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4 on SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128. Windows 11. The output is the same on 11, apart from the digits of 1e: 11.0 converts the `double` to `0.1234567890123456773698862321`, which is still not the client's value.
- I understand that flowing the settings needs public API on a package the docs now call legacy. #2425 (2018) asked for custom serializer settings for patching and was closed for lack of community interest. Even without new API, surfacing the converter's message would help.

Investigation and write-up assisted by Claude (Anthropic); the linked repro was run on Windows 11 (10.0.26200) with .NET SDK 10.0.402, Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 10.0.13 and Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3, and with .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128, Microsoft.AspNetCore.JsonPatch 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 and Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4, and I reviewed this report.

title: MapStaticAssets: builder conventions (e.g. RequireAuthorization) are not applied to the runtime fallback endpoint
body:
## Summary

Conventions added to the builder returned by `MapStaticAssets()` (for example `RequireAuthorization()`) are applied only to the endpoints created from the build manifest. The development runtime fallback endpoint that `MapStaticAssets()` also registers does not receive those conventions, so the two endpoint sets that serve files from the same web root are configured independently.

## What is wrong

* The invariant "conventions added through the `MapStaticAssets()` builder apply to every endpoint that serves static assets" does not hold.
* When the app runs from build output (the fallback is enabled unless `DisableStaticAssetNotFoundRuntimeFallback` is `true`), `StaticAssetDevelopmentRuntimeHandler.EnableSupport` registers a separate catch-all `{**path:file}` endpoint with `MapFallback`. It is not created through the builder returned to the app.
* `StaticAssetsEndpointConventionBuilder` appends conventions to a list that is shared only with `StaticAssetsEndpointDataSource`, and that list is applied lazily to the manifest endpoints. The fallback endpoint never sees it.
* The fallback endpoint only carries a file-exists route constraint, a GET/HEAD method restriction, and the default `MapFallback` metadata. Its delegate clears the selected endpoint and runs the static file middleware, so no endpoint-level metadata (authorization, CORS, rate limiting, response headers, and so on) from the app is in effect for it.
* The environment name is not part of the enablement check (`IsEnabled` looks at the build manifest and the `ReloadStaticAssetsAtRuntime` key), so this is not limited to `Development`.
* The documentation says endpoint-based static asset delivery "works with other endpoint-aware features, such as authorization", and is silent on whether builder conventions apply to the runtime fallback.

## Why it matters (defense in depth)

* Correctness: the behavior of a file served from the web root depends on whether it is reached through a manifest endpoint or through the fallback. App authors reasonably expect a convention applied to `MapStaticAssets()` to cover both.
* Hardening: authorization and similar policies for static assets should be decided in one place and be evaluated before a file is resolved, rather than depend on which endpoint the router happened to select. This strengthens the endpoint-metadata boundary for static assets without needing to reason about how request paths map to files.
* The behavior was observed identically on 9.0.20 and 10.0.12, and the fallback is still registered the same way on `main`.

## Affected code

* src/StaticAssets/src/Development/StaticAssetDevelopmentRuntimeHandler.cs:255-330 - `EnableSupport` registers the fallback via `MapFallback` (line 286), clears the endpoint (line 293), adds the file-exists constraint (line 326) and the GET/HEAD restriction (line 330); the builder is not connected to the fallback
* src/StaticAssets/src/Development/StaticAssetDevelopmentRuntimeHandler.cs:398 - `FileExistsConstraint`
* src/StaticAssets/src/StaticAssetsEndpointConventionBuilder.cs:11-50 - `Add` and `Finally` write only to the lists shared with the manifest endpoint data source
* src/StaticAssets/src/StaticAssetsEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs - `MapStaticAssets` calls `EnableSupport` after building the manifest endpoints
* src/StaticAssets/test/StaticAssetsIntegrationTests.cs - existing development fallback tests (for example `CanServeNewFilesAddedAfterBuildDuringDevelopment`)

## Recommended fix

**Selected approach (A): forward conventions to the fallback.** Give `StaticAssetsEndpointConventionBuilder` an internal way to attach the fallback's `IEndpointConventionBuilder` (for example `AttachFallback`) and have `EnableSupport` call it after the fallback's own conventions are added. `Add` and `Finally` then also forward each convention to every attached fallback builder. Take a snapshot of the attached fallbacks under the existing lock and invoke them outside the lock. Only conventions the app adds after the fallback is attached are forwarded; the internal conventions added earlier (build metadata, hot reload) are not. All new members are `internal`, so no public API change is expected.

Because authorization and other metadata are then evaluated for the fallback endpoint before the file is resolved, the fix does not depend on how a request path is spelled.

Alternatives considered:

| Option | Summary | Why not primary |
|--------|---------|-----------------|
| B | Return 404 from the fallback for files listed in the manifest | Depends on path comparison, can miss alternate spellings of the same file, does not cover files not in the manifest |
| C | Restrict the fallback to the `Development` environment | Reduces exposure but removes behavior for apps that run build output elsewhere; does not make conventions consistent |
| D | Reject request paths that differ from the physical file name | Needs a canonical (handle-based) path lookup on Windows, does not cover files not in the manifest |
| E | Documentation only | Does not change behavior |

A and C can be combined. B and D are possible additional hardening, not substitutes.

Compatibility and risks:

* Conventions are applied lazily on the first request, as for manifest endpoints. Conventions added after endpoints are built are ignored for both, as today.
* A convention that assumes manifest-specific metadata (for example `Metadata.OfType<StaticAssetDescriptor>().Single()`) would now also run against the fallback endpoint and could throw. No such convention was found in the framework sources. Decide whether to skip such conventions for the fallback or document the requirement.
* Calling `MapStaticAssets()` more than once already registers more than one fallback; forwarding must reach every attached fallback.
* Apps that relied on the fallback being unaffected by conventions (for example, intentionally serving new files anonymously while the manifest assets require authorization) will see a behavior change. Call this out in the release notes or a breaking change note.
* Documentation (static files article, runtime configuration options) should state that builder conventions apply to the runtime fallback.

Existing mitigations for apps today:

* Configure a global authorization `FallbackPolicy` that requires an authenticated user.
* Set `DisableStaticAssetNotFoundRuntimeFallback` to `true`.
* Deploy published output, which does not register the runtime fallback.
* Keep files that need protection outside the web root.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] A convention added through the builder returned by `MapStaticAssets()` (both `Add` and `Finally`) is applied to the runtime fallback endpoint as well as the manifest endpoints.
* [ ] `RequireAuthorization()` on `MapStaticAssets()` results in the same authorization outcome for the fallback endpoint as for manifest endpoints.
* [ ] Internal conventions added before the fallback is attached are not forwarded; conventions added by the app after `MapStaticAssets()` returns are.
* [ ] Multiple `MapStaticAssets()` calls forward conventions to every attached fallback.
* [ ] Regression tests in `src/StaticAssets/test/StaticAssetsIntegrationTests.cs` cover forwarded `Add` and `Finally` conventions and an authorization case, and fail without the fix.
* [ ] Behavior with a global `FallbackPolicy` and with `DisableStaticAssetNotFoundRuntimeFallback=true` is unchanged.
* [ ] No public API surface change, or any change goes through API review.
* [ ] Docs are updated to describe how conventions interact with the runtime fallback, with a breaking change note if the behavior change is considered one.

title: URL Rewrite identity rules re-decode `Request.Path`
body:
A rewrite rule that matches `Request.Path` and re-emits the same captured segment (even a no-op/identity rule) can change the path value, because the rule matches against `Request.Path.ToString()` (escaped form) and reassigns via `PathString.FromUriComponent()` (decodes again). A path already containing a literal `%2e` (from Kestrel's normal single decode) becomes `..` after passing through the rule.

**Repro**

```csharp
app.UseRewriter(new RewriteOptions()
    .AddRewrite("^test/(.*)", "test/$1", skipRemainingRules: true));
app.Run(ctx => ctx.Response.WriteAsync(ctx.Request.Path));
```
Request: `GET /test/%252e%252e/secret`
- Before rewrite: `Request.Path` = `/test/%2e%2e/secret`
- After rewrite: `Request.Path` = `/test/../secret`

**Expected:** pass-through rewrite rule should not change `Request.Path`'s value.

title: Certificate forwarding replaces ITlsConnectionFeature without preserving TLS channel binding
body:
## Summary

When certificate forwarding replaces the request's `ITlsConnectionFeature`, the replacement does not implement `TryGetChannelBindingBytes`. The interface default returns `false`, so consumers such as the Negotiate handler observe "no channel binding available" on HTTPS requests whose underlying TLS connection does have one.

## What is wrong

* **Broken invariant:** changing where a request's client certificate comes from should not change the channel binding reported for the underlying connection. Today, the presence of the configured certificate header changes `TryGetChannelBindingBytes(ChannelBindingKind.Endpoint)` from `true` to `false` for the same connection.
* `ITlsConnectionFeature.TryGetChannelBindingBytes` was added in 11.0 (#67436) as a default interface method that returns `false`. Kestrel, HTTP.sys, and IIS in-process override it.
* `CertificateForwardingMiddleware.Invoke` sets a new `CertificateForwardingFeature` whenever the configured header is non-empty. The new feature does not keep the server's original feature, so the default implementation applies.
* Managed Negotiate (#68317) reads the binding from whichever `ITlsConnectionFeature` is current. When it returns `false`, `NegotiateState` constructs `NegotiateAuthentication` without `Binding`, so channel binding is not applied to that authentication exchange.
* The same pattern exists in IIS out-of-process integration (`ForwardedTlsConnectionFeature`) and in the Kestrel `ClientCertBufferingFeature` sample.

## Why it matters (defense in depth)

* **Correctness:** the channel binding result depends on an unrelated middleware and on whether a header is present. Negotiate degrades silently, with no log entry or failure, so the configuration looks protected while it is not.
* **Hardening:** channel binding was added to Negotiate in 11.0 so authentication is tied to the TLS connection. A middleware that only intends to change the client certificate source should not implicitly turn that protection off.
* **Extensibility:** because the method is a default interface member, any wrapper or replacement of `ITlsConnectionFeature` (framework, sample, or third-party) silently drops the binding unless it explicitly delegates.

## Affected code

* [src/Middleware/HttpOverrides/src/CertificateForwardingMiddleware.cs:47-55](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Middleware/HttpOverrides/src/CertificateForwardingMiddleware.cs#L47-L55) - replaces the feature when the header is present
* [src/Middleware/HttpOverrides/src/CertificateForwardingFeature.cs:11-52](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Middleware/HttpOverrides/src/CertificateForwardingFeature.cs#L11-L52) - no `TryGetChannelBindingBytes`, no reference to the original feature
* [src/Http/Http.Features/src/ITlsConnectionFeature.cs:24-53](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Http/Http.Features/src/ITlsConnectionFeature.cs#L24-L53) - default implementation returns `false`
* [src/Security/Authentication/Negotiate/src/NegotiateHandler.cs:413-423](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Security/Authentication/Negotiate/src/NegotiateHandler.cs#L413-L423) - reads the binding from the current feature
* [src/Security/Authentication/Negotiate/src/Internal/NegotiateState.cs:17-33](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Security/Authentication/Negotiate/src/Internal/NegotiateState.cs#L17-L33) - empty token results in no `Binding`
* [src/Servers/IIS/IISIntegration/src/IISMiddleware.cs:145-152](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Servers/IIS/IISIntegration/src/IISMiddleware.cs#L145-L152) - same replacement pattern
* [src/Servers/IIS/IISIntegration/src/ForwardedTlsConnectionFeature.cs:11-52](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Servers/IIS/IISIntegration/src/ForwardedTlsConnectionFeature.cs#L11-L52) - same missing delegation
* [src/Servers/Kestrel/samples/SampleApp/ClientCertBufferingFeature.cs:32-76](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Servers/Kestrel/samples/SampleApp/ClientCertBufferingFeature.cs#L32-L76) - sample wrapper without delegation

## Recommended fix

**Selected approach: delegate channel binding to the original feature.**

* In `CertificateForwardingMiddleware.Invoke`, capture `httpContext.Features.Get<ITlsConnectionFeature>()` before replacing it and pass it to `CertificateForwardingFeature`.
* Implement `TryGetChannelBindingBytes` in `CertificateForwardingFeature` by delegating to the captured feature; return `false` with an empty token when there is none.
* Apply the same change to `IISMiddleware` / `ForwardedTlsConnectionFeature`, and update the Kestrel `ClientCertBufferingFeature` sample to delegate.
* Update the XML docs on `ITlsConnectionFeature.TryGetChannelBindingBytes` to state that implementations which wrap or replace another `ITlsConnectionFeature` must delegate this method.
* Add a debug-level log in `NegotiateHandler` when `Request.IsHttps` is `true` but no channel binding is available, so the degraded mode is observable.

Both feature types are internal, so the selected approach has no public API change.

**Alternatives considered:**

* **Separate channel binding feature** (for example, a dedicated feature interface that certificate middleware never replaces). This is more robust against third-party wrappers, but it is a public API change that needs API review. `TryGetChannelBindingBytes` is still in `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`, so this remains possible before 11.0 GA and is worth discussing.
* **Fail closed in Negotiate** when `Request.IsHttps` is `true` and no binding is available. This would break servers that legitimately do not provide a binding (for example, HTTP.sys with legacy hardening), so it would need an opt-in option, which is also public API.
* **Documentation only.** This leaves the silent degradation in place.

**Compatibility considerations:**

* The delegated binding describes the TLS connection the server terminated (`tls-server-end-point` is derived from that server's certificate). Behind a TLS-terminating proxy, clients compute their binding from the certificate the proxy presented.
* Deployments where the proxy and backend present the same certificate behave the same with or without the forwarded header after the fix.
* Deployments where the certificates differ and Negotiate currently succeeds only because the binding is dropped will start failing after the fix. Owners should decide whether this needs a breaking-change note, documentation that channel binding is not supported behind TLS-terminating proxies, or an opt-out.
* The feature is new in 11.0 and has not shipped in a GA release, so fixing it before 11.0 GA avoids a behavior change after release.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] With certificate forwarding configured and the header present, `TryGetChannelBindingBytes` on the request's `ITlsConnectionFeature` returns the same result and bytes as the server's original feature.
* [ ] When there is no original feature, `TryGetChannelBindingBytes` returns `false` with an empty token.
* [ ] `CertificateForwardingTest` covers delegation with a fake original feature that provides a token, and covers the no-original-feature case.
* [ ] `IISMiddlewareTests` covers the same behavior for `ForwardedTlsConnectionFeature`.
* [ ] A `NegotiateHandlerTests` test runs `UseCertificateForwarding()` before authentication with the header present and asserts the Negotiate state receives the connection's non-empty binding. The test fails before the fix and passes after it.
* [ ] `NegotiateHandler` logs at debug level when an HTTPS request has no channel binding, with a test asserting the log.
* [ ] `ITlsConnectionFeature.TryGetChannelBindingBytes` XML docs describe the delegation requirement.
* [ ] The Kestrel `ClientCertBufferingFeature` sample delegates `TryGetChannelBindingBytes`.
* [ ] The compatibility decision for proxies presenting a different certificate is recorded (release note, docs, or opt-out).

title: Response compression: add a minimum response size threshold (MinimumSize)
body:
Related to #5994. I'd like to work on this, but wanted to check the design with you first.

Right now there's no way to skip compression for small responses, even though the response compression docs say not to compress anything under roughly 150-1000 bytes. Express's compression middleware has a `threshold` option (1kb by default), nginx has `gzip_min_length`, and Spring Boot has `server.compression.min-response-size` (2048 bytes by default). Express is the closest match since it's also a middleware.

My idea is an `int MinimumSize` on `ResponseCompressionOptions`, defaulting to 0 so existing apps behave the same. If Content-Length is known and smaller than that, the response isn't compressed and no Content-Encoding header is added. If there's no Content-Length it's compressed like today, so nothing gets buffered, which is how Tratcher and davidfowl described it in #5994. I'd update PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt and add tests for below, at and above the threshold, plus a streaming case.

There's also #58737, which proposes disabling compression per endpoint and lists a `Predict`-style callback as an alternative design. A callback could cover the size case too by checking Content-Length, but a plain `MinimumSize` is simpler to configure and is what Express, nginx and Spring Boot offer. Would you rather have the threshold on its own, or should this go through the callback approach from #58737?

title: Cookie name matching is case-insensitive, diverging from RFC 6265's case-sensitive semantics
body:
RFC 6265 (§4.1.1, §5.3) specifies that cookie names are matched case-sensitively when a browser stores, updates, or looks up a cookie. ASP.NET Core, however, treats cookie names case-insensitively throughout its cookie-handling APIs. `RequestCookieCollection` parses the incoming `Cookie` header into a dictionary using [`StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/92b29c372eb45d57c415b01b06b41a3a8c439ed6/src/Http/Http/src/Internal/RequestCookieCollection.cs#L30), so   `Request.Cookies["MyCookie"]` and `Request.Cookies["mycookie"]` resolve to the same entry even though a client can legitimately hold two distinct, separately-stored cookies differing only by case.

We need to match RFC and treat cookie case sensitively. We would need to announce a breaking change for consumers about this change.

title: .NET 10 OpenAPI emits an object constraint for floating-point values
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues.

### Describe the bug

With `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` **10.0.12**, enabling `JsonNumberHandling.AllowNamedFloatingPointLiterals` generates an unsatisfiable schema for a `double` property. The endpoint returns numeric values, but its OpenAPI 3.1.1 schema requires an object alongside number/string alternatives:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "anyOf": [
    {
      "pattern": "^-?(?:0|[1-9]\\d*)(?:\\.\\d+)?(?:[eE][+-]?\\d+)?$",
      "type": ["number", "string"]
    },
    {
      "enum": ["NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity"]
    }
  ],
  "format": "double"
}
```

A number fails the object constraint; an object fails both alternatives. No JSON value satisfies this schema.

### Expected Behavior

Keep the numeric and named-literal alternatives without the outer `"type": "object"` constraint.

### Steps To Reproduce

[Reproduction repository](https://github.com/alexaka1/repro-dotnet--aspnetcore-openapi-floating-point)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/alexaka1/repro-dotnet--aspnetcore-openapi-floating-point.git
cd repro-dotnet--aspnetcore-openapi-floating-point
docker compose up --build -d
docker compose run --rm compare
```

The repro changes two things in `dotnet new webapi`: enables `AllowNamedFloatingPointLiterals` through `ConfigureHttpJsonOptions` and changes `WeatherForecast.TemperatureF` from `int` to `double`.

The comparison runs the same source on both versions and prints the response value and `temperatureF` schema.

### Exceptions (if any)

None. Both endpoints return HTTP 200.

### .NET Version

SDK **10.0.401**, ASP.NET Core and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` **10.0.12**.

### Anything else?

| Runtime and OpenAPI package | Native ARM64 | Emulated x64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10.0.12 | Incorrect object constraint | Incorrect object constraint |
| 11.0.0-preview.6.26359.118 | Correct numeric alternatives | Correct numeric alternatives |

The bug is architecture-independent. Each version produced identical documents on native ARM64 and x64 under Docker emulation on an ARM64 host. The .NET 10 containers ran Ubuntu 24.04 and reported `linux-arm64` and `linux-x64`, respectively.

[`OpenApiJsonSchema.ReadProperty`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.12/src/OpenApi/src/Schemas/OpenApiJsonSchema.Helpers.cs#L298-L308) unconditionally sets `schema.Type = JsonSchemaType.Object` when reading `anyOf` or `oneOf`. #67001 removes that assignment as part of union support. The comparison above verifies the corrected behavior in .NET 11 Preview 6.

Could this correction be considered for a .NET 10 servicing release?

title: Add agent guidance for AzDO and Helix CI investigation
body:
## Summary

Add repository-specific Copilot guidance for diagnosing and retrying Azure Pipelines and Helix failures on ASP.NET Core pull requests.

## Motivation and goals

Agent-driven CI investigations currently require rediscovering several ASP.NET Core-specific distinctions that materially affect the correct response to a red aggregate:

- A failed Azure Pipelines aggregate may represent a product/test failure, pre-Helix restore failure, Helix submission failure, post-test reporter failure, merge conflict, or unrelated infrastructure problem.
- GitHub's check-run rerequest endpoint may not support Azure Pipelines external checks.
- A retry should be scoped to the affected pipeline and should occur only after every failure is attributed.

For example, #69232 had two failed `signalr.client.java.Tests--` Helix work items even though every Java test passed. Both failed later in Gradle `:test:testReport` because Spotless could not load JGit `AnyObjectId`. The MVC-only diff had no correlation, and a target-branch build using the same target SHA passed both Windows Helix subsets. A scoped `/azp run aspnetcore-ci` queued a replacement build, which passed along with Build Analysis and Build Insights.

Other recent investigations have encountered materially different red states, including restore failures before any Helix work item was submitted, Helix submission HTTP failures, and merge conflicts where no AzDO build was queued. Durable guidance would make classifications and retry decisions more consistent and evidence-based.

## In scope

- Add a dedicated `.github/instructions/ci.instructions.md` or an equivalent focused section in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
- Require resolving every red aggregate to its exact AzDO build and job and, when present, its Helix work item and failure stage.
- Require correlation with changed files, Build Analysis/known-issue evidence, target-branch comparison, and build progression as applicable.
- Explicitly distinguish product/test failures from restore, submission, reporter, post-test, merge-conflict, and infrastructure failures.
- Document the scoped `/azp run <pipeline-name>` retry path for Azure Pipelines checks when GitHub rerequest is unsupported.
- Require verifying bot acknowledgement, replacement build ID, PR source SHA, and final Build Analysis/Build Insights state.
- Prohibit empty commits as a CI retry mechanism.

## Out of scope

- Changing Azure Pipelines or Helix infrastructure.
- Automatically classifying failures without log evidence.
- Creating or expanding Known Build Error issues.
- Repository-specific guidance for non-AzDO CI systems.

## Risks / unknowns

- Guidance could duplicate or drift from Arcade's Build Analysis documentation; the repository instruction should link to or align with the authoritative workflow rather than restating unstable implementation details.
- Pipeline names and retry-comment behavior may evolve, so examples should emphasize the decision process and scoped retry principle.
- The instruction's `applyTo` scope needs to cover PR/CI maintenance tasks without affecting unrelated code-authoring prompts.

## Examples

Suggested core guidance:

> Do not classify or retry a red Azure Pipelines aggregate until every failure is resolved to its exact build, job, and—when present—Helix work item and failure stage. Correlate the signature with changed files and build progression, compare the target branch and known-issue evidence where needed, and distinguish product/test failures from restore, submission, reporter, post-test, merge-conflict, and infrastructure failures. Retry only after attribution; for external AzDO checks use the repository's scoped `/azp run <pipeline-name>` path when GitHub rerequest is unsupported, and verify the replacement build was actually queued. Never use an empty commit as a retry mechanism.

title: Improve repository agent guidance for recurring workflow failures
body:
## Summary

Document three recurring agent workflow requirements in the repository guidance: locating explicitly requested skills from configured plugin sources, serializing overlapping .NET build/test graphs that share the `artifacts` tree, and bootstrapping the repository SDK when activation reports it missing.

## Motivation and goals

Recent work on #68943 and PR #69233 exposed repeatable failure modes that are not currently stated clearly enough in repository guidance:

- An explicitly required skill was initially treated as unavailable even though it existed in the configured `javiercn/skills` plugin source. This led to an ad hoc substitute workflow and a later redo using the required skill.
- Concurrent focused Output Caching and Response Caching test runs shared the checkout's `artifacts` tree and failed with `CS2012`/file-lock errors. Serial execution passed the same tests, showing the failures came from execution topology rather than the changes under test.
- After repository environment activation reported that the expected SDK was missing, repository bootstrap through `restore.cmd`, followed by reactivation, was required before validation could proceed.

The goal is to make these recovery paths explicit so future agents avoid incorrect substitutions, false build diagnoses, and repeated failed SDK invocations.

## In scope

- Add repository-wide guidance that when a user explicitly requires a named skill and it is not loaded, agents should search configured project and user plugin sources before substituting another workflow.
- Add repository-wide guidance not to run overlapping `dotnet build` or `dotnet test` graphs concurrently in the same checkout unless outputs are isolated or a verified no-build path is used.
- Identify `CS2012`, access-denied, and file-in-use errors during concurrent builds as likely shared-artifact topology failures before diagnosing source changes.
- Document the repository SDK bootstrap sequence: activate the environment; if the SDK is reported missing, run the platform restore script from the repository root; wait for completion; reactivate; retry.

## Out of scope

- Changing build infrastructure or the layout of the shared `artifacts` tree.
- Installing or changing any SDK, package, or NuGet version in repository configuration.
- Adding product-specific cache-key serialization guidance; that can be considered separately if future caching work shows a broader need.
- Defining general runtime behavior for skill discovery outside this repository's agent guidance.

## Risks / unknowns

- Skill discovery guidance should not imply that arbitrary remote sources may be installed or trusted automatically; it should be limited to already configured project/user plugin sources.
- Build concurrency guidance should allow verified isolated-output or no-build scenarios rather than prohibiting all parallel test execution.
- SDK bootstrap wording must remain platform-correct (`restore.cmd` on Windows and `./restore.sh` on Linux/macOS) and should not encourage repeated restoration when the failure has another cause.

## Examples

Possible additions to `.github/copilot-instructions.md`:

- When an explicitly required named skill is unavailable, search configured project and user plugin sources and load it before proceeding; do not silently replace it with an ad hoc workflow.
- Do not run overlapping .NET build/test project graphs concurrently in one checkout when they share the repository `artifacts` tree. Treat `CS2012` and file-lock failures as execution-topology problems first.
- If environment activation reports that the repository SDK is missing, run the platform restore script from the repository root, reactivate the environment, and retry the original command.

Recent ASP.NET Core Copilot sessions repeatedly encountered the same avoidable friction even though the existing repository guidance already covers baseline reproduction, acceptance criteria, red/green testing, faithful behavioral boundaries, SDK activation, and MSBuild configuration matrices.

The recurring gaps were:

1. **Required skills were bypassed when not installed locally.** Multiple sessions were explicitly told to use `explain-changes` or `introspect-session`, but initially substituted a hand-written approximation. The user then had to clarify that the skills were available from `javiercn/skills` and require the skill-driven workflow.
2. **Validation commands selected a wider dependency graph than the changed product required.** Response Caching's Middleware wrapper expanded into unrelated native IIS/googletest prerequisites; a focused gRPC test traversed Blazor-generated assets, native IIS, and an uninitialized submodule; ProjectTemplates' normal area build did not produce its delayed test assembly, while hosted template tests required the full local package graph. In each case, the focused product boundary was valid but had to be discovered after unrelated failures.
3. **PR feedback enumeration required corrective passes.** Sessions needed additional GraphQL/REST queries to include submitted review bodies, suppressed/minimized comments, resolved/outdated inline threads, top-level comments, requested changes, and current-head checks. On #69231, actionable guidance was present in a review body's suppressed comments rather than only in standard inline-thread output.
4. **Red Azure DevOps aggregates did not identify the actionable failure.** On #69231, one run contained a pre-existing Kestrel assertion already fixed on newer `main`; the replacement run contained a different whole-batch timeout (exit 137, no failed assertion) whose exact target baseline passed in 8:14. Other recent gRPC, Identity, and Components.AI sessions likewise needed exact job/work-item attribution to separate unrelated Kestrel/file-lock failures from a genuinely PR-caused dependency-discovery failure.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add concise repository-wide rules to `.github/copilot-instructions.md` covering these four workflows.

#### 1. Honor explicitly requested skills

Proposed guidance:

> When the user explicitly requires a skill that is not installed in the current session, locate it in the available repository or user skill sources (including `javiercn/skills` when applicable), load or install it for the session, and follow its workflow. Do not silently replace a required skill with an unstructured approximation.

#### 2. Select the smallest faithful validation graph

Proposed guidance under **Running tests**:

> Inspect an area's build wrapper before running it. After activating the repository SDK, start with the exact test project or documented focused command when it faithfully exercises the changed surface, then broaden validation deliberately. Area wrappers can expand unrelated projects and require native submodules, generated assets, installers, or a full local package graph.
>
> If validation is blocked by an unrelated prerequisite, name the exact prerequisite and distinguish that boundary from a product build or test failure. Do not claim the broader validation passed, and do not treat the missing prerequisite as evidence that the changed product is broken.

This should complement, not replace, the existing requirement to use area build scripts and the scoped MSBuild guidance in `.github/instructions/build.instructions.md`.

#### 3. Enumerate every PR feedback surface

Proposed guidance:

> Before declaring a PR feedback pass complete, inspect top-level conversation comments, submitted review bodies (including suppressed or minimized content), inline review threads including resolved or outdated threads, requested-changes state, and checks for the current head commit.
>
> Evaluate feedback against the issue contract and current target branch rather than accepting it blindly. For feedback that is incorrect, obsolete, or out of scope, reply with concise evidence and do not broaden the change.
>
> Reply inside each addressed inline review thread and resolve it only after the fix and reply are pushed. Record actionable feedback handled, feedback intentionally not adopted, the resulting head commit, validation, and any unresolved blockers.

#### 4. Require evidence-based AzDO/Helix classification and bounded retries

Proposed guidance:

> Resolve every red aggregate to the exact Azure DevOps build, timeline job, Helix job and work item, exit code, test-result presence, and relevant log evidence before changing code or rerunning CI. Treat Build Analysis classifications and historical rates as investigation leads, not proof.
>
> Correlate each failure with the PR's changed files and build progression. When attribution is unclear, compare the exact target-parent commit used by the PR merge build with a target-branch build of the same job, batch, or test.
>
> Use `/azp run` only after every current failure is accounted for as PR-caused, known, transient, or unrelated. Verify that replacement builds were queued and monitor them to a terminal state. Do not retry an immutable failed Helix monitor result, create an empty commit to rerun CI, or repeatedly retry the same unmatched failure.

### Additional context

This proposal comes from reviewing repeated friction across multiple recent dotnet/aspnetcore implementation, PR-maintenance, and CI-investigation sessions, including merged PR #69231. It intentionally does not duplicate existing instructions for current-main reproduction, acceptance criteria, faithful validation boundaries, per-case red/green verification, repository SDK activation, public API review, or the configuration-matrix rules in `.github/instructions/build.instructions.md`.

The changes are documentation-only. Product-specific cache-accounting and middleware-state testing lessons may be better handled separately in a future scoped `src/Middleware/AGENTS.md`; they are not included here because the repeated repository-wide evidence is stronger for the four workflows above.

A retrospective of recent ASP.NET Core coding-agent sessions found three recurring workflow gaps in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`:

1. **Windows build instructions are contradictory.** `## Running tests` says to use `src/<area>/build.sh -test` unconditionally, although this repository also has area `build.cmd` entry points. 2. **The Windows SourceLink task-host failure lacks a bounded diagnostic path.** The Razor-components session's initial build failed before compilation in `Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git.TranslateRepositoryUrls`; another Grpc investigation (#68639) reported the same pre-compilation MSBuild/SourceLink task-host blocker and could not validate its behavior at runtime. A focused local build succeeded in the first session with `-p:EnableSourceControlManagerQueries=false -p:EnableSourceLink=false`; that is a local diagnostic fallback, not a replacement for normal CI validation.
3. **PR creation can proceed before the worktree branch is published.** The first attempt to create #69569 returned HTTP 422 (`head main, base main`) while its committed, renamed worktree branch had not been pushed. Publishing `HEAD`, checking that no PR existed, and retrying worked. A separate Components owner session for #69484 needed an urgent status check when the branch appeared ready but no PR was visible after several minutes; its exact cause was not established, so the common need is a preflight and explicit failure reporting, not a claim of the same failure.

- Make the **Running tests** entry-point guidance OS-specific: use `src\<area>\build.cmd` on Windows and `src/<area>/build.sh` on Unix, after activating the repo-local SDK. State how to select a specific project/test filter via the area's guidance rather than implying a full area or repository build is always necessary.

## Summary

Add repository-wide Copilot guidance for three recurring agent-workflow failure modes: late compatibility analysis, fresh-worktree build prerequisite thrash, and false-green validation based only on command exit codes.

## Motivation and goals

Recent agent-assisted work in this repository repeatedly encountered gaps that are not explicit in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`:

- In #69237, replacing formatter-based SAN parsing with a typed decoder correctly fixed culture/OS-sensitive parsing, but malformed-input behavior, common-name fallback, and the security/compatibility policy were only fully characterized during review. Similar representation changes involving protected Blazor circuit payloads required repeated clarification of legacy, reconnect, pause/resume, and rolling-upgrade semantics.
- Several fresh-worktree validations spent time reaching unrelated prerequisites before the changed target: missing repository SDK/bootstrap state, submodules, generated JavaScript assets, native dependencies, or `wix.exe`. The eventual useful validation often required a narrower faithful target, but the repository-wide guidance only names the canonical area wrapper.
- A successful exit code can be false-green. Examples include filtered test commands selecting no intended tests, `Pack` succeeding without producing the required package, and builds stopping at unrelated prerequisites before the requested tests execute.

The goal is to make compatibility decisions earlier, reduce repeated build-command experimentation, and require evidence that validation exercised and produced the intended result.

## In scope

- Add guidance under **Task Scope and Completion** requiring compatibility characterization before replacing parsers, formatters, serializers, or protected/persisted payload representations. The characterization should cover valid, malformed, and legacy inputs; exceptions versus fallback; relevant OS/culture differences; rolling upgrades; and downstream security/identity effects.
- Add a **Running tests** preflight for fresh worktrees: read product-area guidance and identify required SDK bootstrap, submodules, generated assets, and native tools before invoking an expensive area build.
- Keep the canonical area build as the first choice, but define a bounded fallback when it fails before reaching the changed target because of an unrelated prerequisite: use the smallest faithful command permitted by product-area guidance and report the exact limitation.
- Require observable validation evidence: the intended nonzero test set ran, required artifacts were produced, and execution reached the relevant assertion or behavior.

## Out of scope

- Changing product code, build scripts, test infrastructure, or CI.
- Replacing product-specific `AGENTS.md`, README, or `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` guidance.
- Treating a narrow fallback as equivalent to the canonical area build or full suite.
- Requiring every worktree to initialize every submodule or build every generated asset when the intended validation path does not need them.

## Risks / unknowns

- The fallback wording must not encourage agents to bypass canonical build scripts prematurely. It should apply only when the canonical path fails before reaching the changed project/test due to a demonstrably unrelated prerequisite.
- Repository-wide wording could duplicate product-specific setup guidance. The proposed rule should require discovering and following that guidance rather than restating individual prerequisites.
- Compatibility analysis can become unbounded. The rule should apply to representation/decoder changes where malformed, legacy, or platform-specific behavior can materially change, not to routine internal refactoring.

## Examples

Possible guidance under **Task Scope and Completion**:

> Before replacing a parser, formatter, serializer, or protected/persisted payload representation, characterize the existing behavior for valid, malformed, and legacy inputs. Include exception versus fallback behavior, platform or culture differences where relevant, rolling-upgrade behavior, and downstream security or identity effects. Resolve the intended compatibility policy before implementation or tests codify the new behavior.

Possible guidance under **Running tests**:

> Before the first build or test in a fresh worktree, read the product-area guidance and identify required repository SDK bootstrap, submodules, generated assets, and native tools. Prepare the prerequisites needed by the intended validation path before invoking an expensive area build.

> If the canonical area build fails before reaching the changed project or test because of an unrelated repository prerequisite, do not repeatedly retry it or describe the affected behavior as validated. Use the smallest faithful product or project command permitted by the product-area guidance, and report both the blocking prerequisite and the narrower validation boundary.

> Verify the observable result of each validation command, not only its exit code. Confirm filtered test commands select the intended nonzero set of tests, pack or build commands produce the required artifacts, and test execution reaches the relevant assertion or behavior.

title: Improve Copilot validation guidance for multi-target and shared-artifact builds
body:
## Summary

Improve `.github/copilot-instructions.md` with repository-specific validation guidance for multi-target projects, shared build artifacts, and targeted-versus-area validation.

## Motivation and goals

A retrospective across recent `dotnet/aspnetcore` agent sessions found three recurring sources of avoidable validation friction:

- A change was validated only on a modern target framework before CI found `net472` compatibility failures (`Enum.IsDefined<TEnum>` and `OperatingSystem.IsWindows`/`IsLinux`) in #69584. Another recent Identity task encountered separate .NET Framework-specific SourceLink/MSBuild behavior.
- Concurrent builds/tests that shared the repository `artifacts` tree produced transient file-lock and `CS2012` failures. Serial execution, including `/m:1` when necessary, passed immediately.
- Broad area build scripts failed on unrelated prerequisites such as absent googletest sources, Blazor JavaScript/template packages, or other generated assets, while targeted project builds faithfully covered the changed managed surface.

The goal is to help Copilot agents choose validation that is complete across declared target frameworks, deterministic around shared outputs, and proportional to the changed surface.

## In scope

- Require inspection of `TargetFrameworks` and compilation of every declared target that is buildable in the current environment before opening or undrafting a pull request.
- Prevent concurrent `dotnet build`/`dotnet test` invocations when project graphs share the repository artifacts tree, with serial `/m:1` recovery guidance for shared-output locks.
- Direct agents to begin with the smallest faithful project validation and escalate to area scripts when broader integration coverage is relevant.
- Require explicit reporting of target frameworks or broader validation boundaries that could not be exercised.

## Out of scope

- Changing repository build scripts, target frameworks, CI configuration, or artifact layout.
- Treating every broad-build failure as unrelated; agents must still determine whether the missing prerequisite is required by the changed behavior.
- Adding a repository-wide rule for manually mapping long test lists to annotations. That caused a mistake in #69584, but the retrospective did not find recurrence in other recent sessions, so it is not yet supported as a durable repository instruction.
- Changing the existing requirement to activate the repository .NET environment before running `dotnet` commands.

## Risks / unknowns

- “Every declared target” must remain qualified by what can be built in the current environment; otherwise agents may spend time attempting unsupported platform-specific targets.
- Targeted validation must not become an excuse to skip required area-level or end-to-end coverage. The proposed wording explicitly requires escalation when broader integration coverage is relevant.
- Some invocations may be safe in parallel when outputs are isolated. The guidance should prohibit only project graphs sharing the repository artifacts tree and allow verified isolated/no-build invocations.
- The current instruction that says to use each area’s `build.sh` may appear to conflict with targeted-first validation. The wording should clarify validation order rather than remove area-script expectations.

## Examples

Proposed additions under `## Running tests` in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`:

```markdown
* Start validation with the smallest project build/test that faithfully covers the changed surface, then escalate to the area build script when its broader integration coverage is required. If an area script fails only because an unrelated native submodule, generated asset, or package prerequisite is absent, record that boundary and continue with targeted project validation; do not repeatedly rerun or provision unrelated prerequisites unless the changed behavior depends on them.
* When a changed project declares multiple target frameworks, inspect its `TargetFrameworks` and compile every declared target that can be built in the current environment before opening or undrafting a pull request. A successful build or test run for only the newest target does not establish compatibility with `net4xx` or other declared targets; explicitly report any target that could not be validated.
* Do not run `dotnet build` or `dotnet test` concurrently for project graphs that share the repository artifacts tree. Run them sequentially, or use a verified isolated/no-build invocation; when a shared-output file lock occurs, retry the smallest targeted command serially (use `/m:1` for MSBuild when needed) before treating it as a product failure.
```

A typical agent workflow after this change would be:

1. Inspect the changed project’s declared target frameworks.
2. Build/test the smallest projects that faithfully cover the change, serializing invocations that share outputs.
3. Compile every locally buildable declared target.
4. Escalate to the area script when integration coverage is required.
5. Report unsupported targets or unrelated prerequisite boundaries explicitly.

title: Clarify Copilot guidance for framework-only invariants vs user-reachable validation
body:
<!--
This template is useful to build consensus about whether work should be done, and if so, the high-level shape of how it should be approached. Use this before fixating on a particular implementation.
-->

## Summary

Update `.github/copilot-instructions.md` to require classifying who can violate a precondition before changing an internal assertion into a runtime exception. Preserve framework-only assertions and their release behavior unless there is evidence that application-controlled input can reach the condition or an explicit contract calls for a runtime failure.

## Motivation and goals

In #68961, commit `6c10ebb2a713b616cdc4d4afcccc3c7d6fdfef28` replaced a `Debug.Assert` in `EndpointHtmlRenderer.InitializeStandardComponentServicesAsync` with an `InvalidOperationException`, and added a test expecting the exception. This condition describes a framework-controlled call-order invariant: the first initialization call owns endpoint-specific data. The existing assertion catches a framework developer mistake during development; in release, a later call reused the cached task. The new throw instead introduces a runtime failure path for that invariant.

The [cross-cutting guidance](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/docs/CrossCuttingGuidance.md) correctly asks for exceptions for invalid public/external input, but the Copilot instructions do not distinguish such validation from an invariant exclusively controlled by framework code. An unqualified preference for surfacing errors can therefore encourage this change. The goal is to make the ownership and reachability check explicit, not to discourage legitimate runtime validation.

## In scope

- Add a concise rule under **Task Scope and Completion** or a dedicated **Assertions and validation** section of `.github/copilot-instructions.md`: before adding a throw or replacing a `Debug.Assert`, trace the callers and identify whether application/user input can cause the violation, or whether it requires framework code to break its own call-order/state invariant.
- For framework-only invariants, retain the development-time assertion and the existing release behavior by default. Do not introduce a new runtime throw or a test that codifies it solely to make the invariant fail loudly in release. If a runtime failure is intentional, explain the reachable scenario and why the behavior change is needed.
- For public/API arguments, configuration, external input, and supported application-driven invalid states, keep runtime validation and actionable exceptions. `internal` visibility by itself does **not** prove that a condition is framework-only.
- When reviewing a replacement assertion, compare Debug and Release behavior and use a test at a faithful caller boundary to establish reachability rather than treating a direct call to an internal helper with impossible arguments as proof of a user scenario.

Suggested instruction text:

> Distinguish framework-controlled invariants from invalid states reachable through supported application/user input before adding an exception or replacing `Debug.Assert`. Trace the real callers and contract. For a condition that only framework code can violate, preserve the assertion and existing Release behavior unless a deliberate runtime behavior change is justified; do not add a throw merely to harden that internal path. Keep runtime exceptions for invalid public/external inputs and supported application-controlled states. A direct test invocation of an internal method does not, by itself, establish user reachability.

## Out of scope

- Changing shipping code or tests in #68961 as part of this documentation issue.
- A blanket ban on exceptions in internal methods, or removal of existing validation for reachable invalid inputs.

## Risks / unknowns

An overbroad reading could suppress needed runtime checks in internal code reached from public APIs. The instruction must key off the source of the invalid state and supported call paths, not method accessibility. It should allow a deliberate exception when a concrete reachable scenario and intended behavior are documented.

## Examples

In `EndpointHtmlRenderer.InitializeStandardComponentServicesAsync`, a second framework-owned initialization supplying endpoint-specific values should remain a `Debug.Assert` while returning the cached task in Release, absent evidence of a supported app-controlled route to that call. By contrast, an invalid argument supplied through a public entry point should still receive a precise runtime exception.

title: Bound aggregate in-flight response buffering in Response Caching
body:
Response Caching caps each request’s cache buffer with `MaximumBodySize`, while `SizeLimit` applies only to completed cache entries. Concurrent requests to a large cacheable endpoint can therefore exceed `SizeLimit` in aggregate - for example, 16 requests buffering an 8 MB (under 64 MB default) response may temporarily use about 128 MB despite a 100 MB (default value) cache limit.

`Cache-Control: no-cache` makes this more noticeable because it bypasses cache lookup while still allowing the response to be buffered and stored. Consider bounding aggregate in-flight buffering or avoiding redundant buffering when an entry already exists.

Title: [Backport request][security] PR #65765 (HTTP/2 trailer Content-Length mismatch → connection-level GOAWAY) is not in any supported release — verified live on 8.0.31, 9.0.20, 10.0.12

## Summary

PR #65765 ("fix HTTP/2: Content-Length mismatch with trailers split across CONTINUATION frames", merged to main ~Nov 2025) prevents a stream-level error from escaping `DecodeTrailersAsync` as a connection-level error. **This fix has not been backported to any supported servicing branch.** I verified today (2026-09-28):

- **v8.0.31, v9.0.20, v10.0.12 source tags** all ship the pre-fix `DecodeTrailersAsync` (no try/catch).
- **Live repro on 10.0.12** (deterministic, 9/9 trials): see below.
- **11.0.0-rc.1 is fixed** (same repro → stream RST only, other streams unaffected).

## Live repro (simpler than the original — no CONTINUATION required)

On any HTTP/2 connection (h2c or h2), send one request:

1. `HEADERS` (stream 1, END_HEADERS, **no** END_STREAM): `:method: POST`, `:path: /A`, `:scheme: http`, `:authority: h`, `content-length: 12`
2. `DATA` (stream 1, no END_STREAM): 5 bytes (less than declared)
3. `HEADERS` (stream 1, END_STREAM | END_HEADERS): **any trailer — e.g. just `x-t: 1`** (a benign trailer suffices; the original repro split trailers across CONTINUATION, but a single trailer HEADERS frame triggers it)
4. `HEADERS` (stream 3, END_STREAM): a valid `GET /` marker request

**Result on 10.0.12:** stream 1 gets `RST_STREAM(PROTOCOL_ERROR)` **and the server sends `GOAWAY(PROTOCOL_ERROR)`, terminating the entire connection** — the stream-3 marker dies with it.
**Result on 11.0.0-rc.1:** stream 1 `RST_STREAM` only; stream 3 completes with 200. ✔

Trigger conditions isolated: the declared `content-length` must exceed the DATA sent, and END_STREAM must arrive via the trailer HEADERS frame. With matching CL + trailers, or with the mismatch ended via a final DATA frame instead, behavior is correctly stream-level on all versions.

## Impact

Any single malformed request kills **all concurrently multiplexed streams** on the connection. Behind a front-end that multiplexes multiple clients over shared upstream H2 connections (envoy/nginx keepalive upstreams, internal meshes), one malicious request can terminate other users' in-flight streams — a cross-user denial of service (same impact model as the Rapid Reset class). The bug and its fix are already publicly documented in #65765; the gap is purely that no supported release contains the fix.

## Ask

Please backport #65765 to 10.0.x, 9.0.x, and 8.0.x servicing. Related: #69574 (my earlier backport request for #66669/#67584 — also verified absent from LTS). Happy to share the raw-socket repro script.

title: [Backport request] Enforce RFC 9113 connection-specific header rejection on .NET 10 LTS — transfer-encoding/keep-alive/proxy-connection/upgrade still accepted in HTTP/2 requests
body:
## Summary

PRs #66669 ("HTTP 2/3: treat messages containing connection-specific header fields malformed — make http2 compliant to RFC 9113 8.2.2") and #67584 ("Reject connection-specific headers sent via HPACK/QPACK indexed names") expanded `IsConnectionSpecificHeaderField` to reject `transfer-encoding`, `keep-alive`, `proxy-connection`, and `upgrade` in HTTP/2 requests. That enforcement is currently only in main (.NET 11). On the .NET 10 LTS line, only `connection` and non-trailers `te` are enforced.

Verified today (2026-09-03), identically on **10.0.11 and 10.0.12** (Linux containers, Kestrel `h2c` listener): an HTTP/2 request carrying any of these headers is **accepted and surfaced to application headers**, in both representations:
- literal new name (`transfer-encoding: chunked`, `keep-alive: 1`, `proxy-connection: 1`, `upgrade: websocket`) → 200, app sees the header;
- HPACK static-name-indexed (`transfer-encoding` is static index 57) → 200.

Controls on the same connections: `connection: keep-alive` → connection error (enforced), `te: chunked` / `te: trailers, gzip` → connection error (enforced), `te: trailers` → accepted (correct).

## Why it matters

`transfer-encoding` surviving into an H2 request (and being surfaced to the application) is exactly the header-confusion primitive #67584's description calls out ("allowing Transfer-Encoding: chunked through on HTTP/2"). The direct exploitability in Kestrel-as-origin is limited (framing in H2 is DATA-based, and my differential campaigns show no framing divergence vs nginx/HAProxy), but any ASP.NET app that *forwards* requests downstream (reverse-proxy patterns; well-behaved forwarders strip hop-by-hop headers, but user-built ones often copy headers) can re-emit both `transfer-encoding` and a computed `content-length` into an HTTP/1 request to an internal service — the classic H2→H1 desync setup. Enforcing the MUST on the LTS line removes the ambiguity at the edge.

## Ask

Please consider backporting #66669 + #67584 to 10.0.x servicing (and 8.0.x/9.0.x if the same gap exists there — I have not verified those lines). If a backport is deemed a breaking change for LTS, an opt-in switch (defaulting to current behavior) would still close the gap for security-sensitive deployments.

## Repro (10.0.12, Kestrel h2c on :5084)

Any raw H2 client (e.g., nghttp or a hand-rolled socket client) sending:

```
HEADERS (stream 1, END_STREAM):
  :method: GET, :scheme: http, :path: /, :authority: h
  transfer-encoding: chunked        <- literal name, OR static-name-index 57
```

→ 200 + request reaches middleware with `Request.Headers["Transfer-Encoding"] == "chunked"`. nginx 1.31.5 rejects the same request with 400.

Happy to provide the full harness/scripts if useful.

[API Proposal] Add HttpConnectionOptions.LogMessageContent for SignalR client diagnostics
body:
## Background and Motivation

Originating issue: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/44383

The issue requests access to the raw data behind SignalR C# client parsing failures. The triage direction is to provide the raw-message diagnostics already available in the JavaScript client.

The implementation adds an explicit opt-in on HTTP connection options. Content is logged at Trace level before Hub protocol parsing, allowing an application to inspect malformed data without replacing its Hub protocol. Implementation commit: https://github.com/ziyiding-ms/aspnetcore/commit/94768bd0d54762b08555855329c829da0aa8aeed. Implementation PR: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69560. No API approval is claimed, and an API-review champion has not yet been assigned.

## Usage Examples

```csharp
var connection = new HubConnectionBuilder()
    .WithUrl("https://example.com/chat", options =>
    {
        options.LogMessageContent = true;
    })
    .ConfigureLogging(logging =>
    {
        logging.SetMinimumLevel(LogLevel.Trace);
        logging.AddConsole();
    })
    .Build();
```

The default is `false`. When enabled, WebSockets, Server-Sent Events and Long Polling log sent and received transport chunks. Each entry logs at most the first 1,024 bytes and includes the original length, recorded length and truncation status. This limit does not truncate the actual transport payload.

Printable ASCII bytes remain readable. Backslashes are escaped and other bytes use `\xHH`, allowing partial UTF-8 sequences and binary data to be represented without decoding them as complete characters. A log entry is a transport chunk, not necessarily a complete Hub message.

## Proposed API

```diff
namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections.Client
{
    public class HttpConnectionOptions
    {
+        public bool LogMessageContent { get; set; }
    }
}
```

## Alternative Designs

- The originating issue suggests displaying content from `JsonHubProtocol.ParseMessage` on errors. Transport-boundary logging instead observes bytes before parsing and works with more than one Hub protocol.
- Recording entire chunks would match the JavaScript client's unbounded content output more closely. The implementation limits each entry to 1,024 input bytes and marks truncation to bound per-entry formatting work.
- Decoding each read as UTF-8 would make intact non-ASCII text easier to read, but byte escapes preserve fragments and binary data without decoder state.

## Risks

Content may contain application data, as the option's XML documentation states. It therefore defaults to off and also requires Trace logging. Enabling it adds string formatting and allocation proportional to the recorded prefix; the per-entry limit does not cap the total number of entries. It is a diagnostic view: truncated entries omit the remainder and chunk boundaries do not identify full Hub messages.

The existing transport behavior remains the default. Runtime tests cover macOS Arm64, not Windows or browser execution.

## Source Justifications

- Raw-message diagnostics are requested: issue #44383, "the entire message payload should be shown to the user or at least if tracing is turned on this should be the behaviour."
- Alignment with JavaScript is the issue's triage direction: "We should do the same thing we do in the JS client and log the raw messages."
- Default and data caution: proposed `HttpConnectionOptions` XML documentation, "Defaults to false. Message contents can contain sensitive application data."
- Scope and bound: proposed XML documentation, "Each entry records at most the first 1,024 bytes of a transport data chunk" and "This option applies to WebSockets, Server-Sent Events, and Long Polling."
- Independent log value: `TransportContentLog`, "The logging state owns a string, never a reference to transport-owned memory."
- Gating: both helper overloads return before formatting when `!enabled || !logger.IsEnabled(LogLevel.Trace) || data.IsEmpty`.
- Payload preservation and parser-failure coverage: `HubConnectionTests.MessageContent.cs` invokes an Echo method with a message larger than the log limit and exercises malformed incoming JSON.

## Triage metadata

The `api-suggestion` and `api-proposal` labels are present. Issue type: `Feature`. An API-review champion has not been assigned; a maintainer champion is requested to take this proposal through API review. Implementation PR #69560 is ready for review. No API approval is claimed.
